@DzmitryShylovich Yeah, absolute paths work just fine. Problem comes when used **relative path**. It's necessary to use relative path for example in case of reusable module with own navigation bar and which is connected to components tree on quite deep level. It's not very handy to  provide variable with path from the root.
https://angular.io/docs/ts/latest/guide/router.html#!#relative-navigation
It seems to me that I did everything right according to docs. Maybe I missed something. But... @DzmitryShylovich Did you manage to see that links look like `/a/(a)` and `/a/(b)`

I have the same problem. It still doesn't work properly in templates.

Hello, I have the same problem. If there is a route **localhost/parent/child** and I have a `[routerLink]="[../sibling]"` link, it creates the url **localhost/parent/child/sibling** instead of **localhost/parent/sibling**.

The only way to get the desired behavior is to use absolute links, which is undesirable with standalone modules. 

The problem occurs only if I use a module with links to sub-modules. For example an authorization module with a login module, sing up module etc. I can not link from the sign up module to the login module without using absolute links. If I change the routing to only use the components (LoginComponent, RegisterComponent) and all these are accessible from the authorization module, the relative links work.

Can confirm that we're seeing the same issue as @leon with pathless routes breaking relative routerLink calls. Adding a path value fixes it, so it's definitely a bug. Using absolute paths for now until this is resolved.
I'm facing this issue too (angular 2 final release)

Imho the routerlink relative path should not look at the actual url tree you create to build your routes, as you regurarly add empty paths to add resolves etc... So it should not depend on that, the relative routerlink should depend on the actual url created from the tree.

We now have broken links everytime we add a level for resolves that depend on each other....

So I think it works as designed, but it's designed badly....
Still seeing this error with Angular 4.2.4. Using absolute links is pretty annoying indeed.

## I'm submitting a ... 

[ ] Regression (behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[x] Bug report 
[ ] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
## Current behavior Given the following routing: * Route `'parent'` * Route `'child'` * Route `''` with component `TestComponent` If the component `TestComponent` tries to programmatically navigate to itself with some parameters (e.g. `/parent/child -> /parent/child;foo=123`) using `relativeTo`, the navigation fails with the following error: this.router.navigate(['.', {foo: 123}], {relativeTo: this.route}); ``` ERROR TypeError: Cannot read property 'path' of undefined at createNewSegmentGroup (create_url_tree.ts:290) at updateSegmentGroup (create_url_tree.ts:295) at createUrlTree (create_url_tree.ts:47) at Router.createUrlTree (router.ts:433) at Router.navigate (router.ts:495) at TestComponent.navigateRelative (app.ts:38) at Object.eval [as handleEvent] (TestComponent.html:2) at handleEvent (view.ts:142) at callWithDebugContext (services.ts:815) at Object.debugHandleEvent [as handleEvent] (services.ts:411) ``` ## Expected behavior The navigation should work. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions *Full Working Example* http://plnkr.co/edit/z4CtoWaDNJMWLAfYKnoP 1. Open the Plunkr and launch the application in a separate window 2. Click on "Navigate Relative" 3. Open the browser console and inspect the error Note: If you click on "Navigate Absolute", which performs an absolute navigation, it works as intended. *Details* 1. Create the following routing configuration: ``` export const APP_ROUTES: Routes = [ { path: 'parent', children: [ { path: 'child', children: [ { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', component: TestComponent } ] } ] } ]; ``` 2. In `TestComponent`, call the method `navigateRelative`: ``` @Component(....) export class TestComponent { constructor(private router: Router, private route: ActivatedRoute) { } navigateRelative(): void { this.router.navigate(['.', {foo: 123}], {relativeTo: this.route}); } } ``` 3. Observe the error described above. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? Relative navigation to myself with different parameters should work. If the path is not empty, it works as well. ## Please tell us about your environment 

Angular version: 4.2.6


Browser: all
